timeline.message:
Use Iterator.remove when trimming cache so even keys violating equals() can be used here.
Fixes #2532
timeline.author: Kevin Read

## Description
<!-- Please describe the changes you made on a high level. -->
<!-- Make sure you reference the GitHub issue here if this change is related to one. -->
Instead of explicitly removing a key from the LruCache (which fails if the key class violates the equals() contract) call remove() on the iterator instead.

## Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!-- If it's fixing a bug reference it or provide repro steps. -->
Using this even cache keys violating equals() can be used here. Fixes #2532.

is there a chance of `ConcurrentModificationException` because of this line?

reply.body: No, using the Iterator to remove is safe when using the Iterator itself to loop over the collection. I added another commit to ensure that we don't overrun the collection, although I don't see how it could happen unless the size to trim to is <0. Can't hurt though I guess.
@unverbraucht thoughts? I don't think we typically have concurrent modifications like this, but it's probably possible (and may be why the code was written the way it was initially).
@sjudd @TWiStErRob good point. It might make sense then to get a fresh instance of the Iterator after every loop run. I've committed proposed changes for that.

timeline.message: Ensure that we don't overrun the iterator
